jobs.title: Software Engineer III, Performance
jobs.description:
### **Minimum qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.
* 2 years of experience with software development in one or more programming languages.
* 2 years of experience with computer architecture, performance analysis, and performance modeling.
* Experience experimenting with AI agents or LLM-powered agentic workflows.
* Experience in systems engineering.

  

### **Preferred qualifications:**

* Master's degree or PhD in Computer Science or related technical fields.
* Experience with low-level accelerator programming (e.g., CUDA, Triton, Pallas) and performance tuning techniques.
* Experience with machine learning, compiler optimization, code generation, and runtime systems for GPU architectures (OpenXLA, MLIR, Triton, etc).
* Debugging experience to improve performance of single-mode or multi-mode (distributed) systems.
* Expertise in tailoring algorithms and ML models to exploit ML accelerator architecture strengths and minimize weaknesses.
* Deep understanding of modern ML accelerator architectures (Nvidia/AMD GPUs, TPUs, Trainium, Cerebras, etc.), memory hierarchies, and performance bottlenecks.

**About the job**
-----------------

Google's software engineers develop the next-generation technologies that change how billions of users connect, explore, and interact with information and one another. Our products need to handle information at massive scale, and extend well beyond web search. We're looking for engineers who bring fresh ideas from all areas, including information retrieval, distributed computing, large-scale system design, networking and data storage, security, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, UI design and mobile; the list goes on and is growing every day. As a software engineer, you will work on a specific project critical to Google’s needs with opportunities to switch teams and projects as you and our fast-paced business grow and evolve. We need our engineers to be versatile, display leadership qualities and be enthusiastic to take on new problems across the full-stack as we continue to push technology forward.

Our team is delivering state-of-the-art performance on OSS models to showcase the capabilities TPUs, to both in industry competitions and to optimize these models so our public customers can leverage the optimization recipes in their own models.

Google Cloud accelerates every organization’s ability to digitally transform its business and industry. We deliver enterprise-grade solutions that leverage Google’s cutting-edge technology, and tools that help developers build more sustainably. Customers in more than 200 countries and territories turn to Google Cloud as their trusted partner to enable growth and solve their most critical business problems.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.
  
  
US: $147000 - $210000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits  
  
Learn more about benefits at Google.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* Write product or system development code. Manually optimize models, using state-of-the-art techniques (sharding, quantization, custom kernels).
* Develop principles from manual optimizations which can be automated via agentic AI (e.g., compute, communication, scheduling, or quantization cost models).
* Land identified principles and recipes to build scalable solutions, for example, by collaborating with the compiler team on cost modeling or by building agentic tooling for headroom analysis.
* Create scalable solutions to serve the third-party customer base by improving out-of-the-box software performance and open-sourcing tooling to external customers.
* Develop trend analysis to identify performance issues in yet-unseen models, solving performance problems before they occur. While maintaining model benchmarks to ensure tracking of performance wins.

jobs.title: Research Scientist / Research Engineer, Search - Knowledge Graphs
jobs.description:
Foundations - San Francisco

  

### **About the Team**

The Foundations Research team works on high-risk, high-reward ideas that could shape the next decade of AI. Our goal is to advance the science and data that enable our training and scaling efforts, with a particular focus on future frontier models. We push the boundaries of data, scaling laws, optimization techniques, model architectures, model + search co-design and efficiency improvements to propel our science.

The Search team sits within Foundationsation.

### **About the Role**

We’re looking for a Researcher to work on semi-structured knowledge graphs within Search. You’ll research and develop methods for mining structured information from heterogeneousation more accessible and useful to AI models.

The core questions are: What structure helps models find and use information? How can we extract it reliably at web scale? And how do we measure whether it improves the model’s ability to reason and answer questions? How do we design the system to be optimizable end-to-end?

You’ll work across research, data, and systems, exploring how advances in AI and compute can improve the way knowledge is extracted, organized, and retrieved. This work will support retrieval across OpenAI products and internal research efforts, with opportunities for scientific publication.

### **Responsibilities**

* Develop methods to extract and connect structured information across diverse web sources, including entities, attributes, and relationships.
* Build scalable approaches for transforming noisy, inconsistent content into useful knowledge representations.
* Explore how models and compute can improve extraction quality and reduce the manual work involved in building knowledge systems.
* Design evaluations that measure both the quality of extracted knowledge and its usefulness for retrieval and model reasoning.
* Partner with researchers and engineers to integrate structured knowledge into Search and use model performance to guide improvements.

### **You Might Thrive in This Role If You Have**

* Deep experience in knowledge extraction, knowledge graphs, entity resolution, or related work that derives structure from large, heterogeneous datasets.
* Strong machine learning and research skills, with experience developing and evaluating methods for real-world data.
* A track record of building or scaling data and ML systems, particularly for web-scale extraction, indexing, or retrieval.
* Experience independently driving open-ended technical problems from an initial idea through experimentation and implementation.
* A first-principles approach to using AI and compute, with a willingness to rethink established methods as model capabilities improve.
* A strong interest in how the representation of information shapes what models can find, understand, and use.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Generalist, Simulation
jobs.description:
**What to Expect**

Full autonomy is of critical importance to Tesla's mission. As a member of TeslaSI’s Simulation team, you will be in a unique position to accelerate the pace at which Autopilot improves over time. The main ways in which the simulation team realizes this is through building tools that enable TeslaSI developers to perform virtual test drives instead of real ones, testing all Autopilot software releases for regressive behavior and generating synthetic data sets for neural network training.

The foundation on which we build these elements is our simulation environment. We develop photorealistic worlds for our virtual car to drive in, enabling our developers to iterate faster and rely less on real-world testing. We strive for perfect correlation to real-world vehicle behavior and work with TeslaSI Software Engineers to improve both Autopilot and the simulator over time. Our group is a cross-disciplinary team with people from various backgrounds and fields of expertise, like CS generalists, mechanical engineers, game developers, and computer graphics artists. As a member on this team, you will be challenged to learn about all these different disciplines and use your own expertise to further improve the scope and usability of our tools.

As a Simulation Engineer, you will contribute to the development of TeslaSI simulation by enabling and supporting the creation of photo realistic 3D scenes that can accurately model the driving experience in a wide range of locales and conditions.

 **What You'll Do**

* Contribute to the development of a modular, scalable simulation platform
* Work with all members of the TeslaSI team to understand the simulation requirements and develop tools to meet those needs
* Enhance the realism and performance of our in-house GPU ray tracer
* Implement algorithms enabling real-time rendering of realistic scenes with complex lighting environments
* Improve existing tools and features that enable the reproduction in Autopilot behavior in simulation

  
**What You'll Bring**

* Extensive knowledge of light transport, appearance models, and color science
* Experience researching, developing, and optimizing state of the art ray tracing techniques such as next even estimation (NEE), reservoir importance sampling (RIS), and multiple importance sampling (MIS)
* Knowledge of modern graphics APIs and shader languages
* Experience working with training frameworks and understanding of modern machine learning concepts
* Experience with optimization across CPU and GPU
* Confidence with modern C++
* Experience with modern physically based rendering engines
* Excellent mathematics skills, including proficiency with linear algebra, calculus, and probability
* Deep understanding of tradeoffs in engine performance, scalability, and maintainability
Experience with supporting tools, such as exporters, terrain editors, and GPU debuggers

You will work at the intersection of compilers, runtime, hardware, and ML frameworks, collaborating with cross-functional partners to deliver a high-quality developer experience for Meta's custom AI accelerators.  
  
  

### **Software Engineer, Systems ML Responsibilities:**

* Lead the design and development of MTIA's profiling and debugging tooling, including performance profiling, live debugging, and core dump for accelerator workloads
* Build tooling capabilities spanning performance profiling, kernel-level diagnostics, and multi-rank fault isolation

jobs.title: Research Engineer, Algorithms
jobs.description:
**Normal Computing | Build with Us**
------------------------------------

Normal is an applied AI company solving the hardest problems in AI and silicon. We build foundational hardware and software for the semiconductor industry, critical AI infrastructure, and the broader systems that power our world, in partnership with the world's most advanced institutions. We work as one team across New York City, Silicon Valley (Mountain View), London, Copenhagen, and Seoul.

**The Role**
------------

Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. You will develop the computational methods that make LLM inference run efficiently on it. The core challenge is rethinking how operations like attention, memory access, and long-context decoding should behave on hardware that computes inside memory, rather than adapting standard GPU kernels to a new chip.

Your job is to develop the algorithms that exploit this natively: understand which parts of LLM workloads are best suited to in-memory execution, design numerical methods that map onto the hardware's physical behavior, and validate them against our simulators and FPGA prototypes first, and against silicon as it arrives.

This is a co-design role. The hardware and the algorithms are developed in parallel, which means you will influence architectural decisions rather than implement against a fixed specification. The strongest candidates have a deep understanding of both large model inference and the mathematics of stochastic systems, and have built systems that run on real hardware.

**What You Will Own**
---------------------

* **Algorithm Development:** Develop algorithms for LLM inference workloads running on our in-memory hardware. Success means algorithms that measurably improve LLM inference on our hardware, demonstrated in simulation and then on silicon.
* **Software/Hardware Co-Design:** Work directly with hardware and architecture teams to shape what the chip can and should compute natively.
* **Numerical Methods:** Design numerical methods that exploit thermal noise and analog dynamics rather than working around them.
* **Evaluation & Benchmarks:** Build evaluation frameworks and benchmarks that characterize algorithm behavior on real hardware or simulation.
* **Workload Translation:** Translate insights about model workloads into constraints and opportunities for hardware design.
* **Rapid Prototyping:** Prototype and iterate rapidly as hardware evolves from simulation to silicon.
* **Performance Optimization:** Optimize performance at both the gate level and the algorithmic level.

**What Makes You a Great Fit**
------------------------------

* Deep understanding of large model inference: attention mechanisms, KV cache, long-context decoding, memory bandwidth constraints
* Experience with inference optimization: quantization, sparsity, kernel fusion, or memory-efficient attention
* Familiarity with stochastic systems, probabilistic methods, numerical analysis, or analog computation
* Experience implementing algorithms close to hardware, beyond high-level frameworks
* Comfort reasoning from first principles about what a novel substrate can do efficiently
* Track record of taking ideas from theory to working implementation on real hardware
* Strong programming skills in Python and at least one systems language
* Collaborative instinct and ability to work across hardware, architecture, and software teams

**Bonus Points**
----------------

* PhD in machine learning, applied mathematics, physics, electrical engineering, or a related field
* Exposure to analog or mixed-signal systems, in-memory compute, or non-von-Neumann architectures
* Experience working on hardware that did not yet exist when you joined
* Publications or open-source work in efficient inference, stochastic algorithms, or novel computing

***Equal Employment Opportunity Statement***

*Normal Computing is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected status.*

*Normal Computing is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please let us know at accommodations@normalcomputing.com.*

*By submitting your application, you agree that Normal Computing may collect, use, and store your personal information for employment-related purposes in accordance with our* *Applicant Privacy Notice**.*

jobs.description:
Meta Robotics Studio builds consumer humanoid robots that bring Meta's AI into the physical world. Our robots run on NVIDIA Jetson Thor with Meta-designed carrier boards and JetPack OS. The Robotics OS team owns everything between the silicon and the robot learning stack. On one chip, our robots run real-time control loops over EtherCAT while large vision-language-action (VLA) models run on the GPU. Our job is to make that computer do both, deterministically, every time it boots.We are hiring a software engineer to help architect and evolve the robotics OS, Meta's build of NVIDIA Jetson Linux for Thor-class robot compute. Working with the team, you will help shape the multi-year technical direction for the robot's operating system, including how we build, release and update it, how it shares one computer between real-time control and AI workloads, and how it scales from a lab of prototypes to a large fleet of production robots. You will work closely with hardware, firmware, controls, and AI engineers across Meta, and with NVIDIA's Jetson engineering teams as one of several technical points of contact on the platform. This is a hands-on role: when a new board spin won't boot or the control loop misses a deadline, you will be in the kernel log alongside the rest of the team.  
  
  

### **Software Engineer, Embedded BSP/Kernel (Robotics OS) Responsibilities:**

* Contribute to the technical strategy and multi-year roadmap for the Robotics OS. This covers the board support package (BSP), kernel, OS image, update system, real-time behavior, GPU platform, and fleet tooling across every robot program and compute platform (AGX Thor, IGX Thor, and future NVIDIA silicon)
* Architect the next-generation OS image, including the move to a Yocto / meta-tegra based build. Make it reproducible, hermetic and secure, and make it fast for many engineers to iterate on
* Define and drive the production update strategy: atomic A/B and over-the-air updates, rollback, secure and verified boot, fusing and signing, and factory provisioning, so we can ship to a growing fleet safely
* Shape the platform's real-time architecture. Help define how CPU cores, interrupts, memory and the GPU are divided between control loops at kilohertz rates and large AI models. Set the latency budgets and the measurement infrastructure that proves we meet them
* Collaborate with NVIDIA's Jetson engineering teams alongside other Meta engineers: share requirements, push fixes upstream, and help plan how we adopt new Jetson Linux / JetPack releases with minimal fork debt
* Partner with electrical, firmware, and mechanical engineers on new compute and carrier-board designs. Weigh in early on SoC configuration, interfaces, power and thermal so boards are easier to bring up and software stays simpler
* Drive bring-up of new boards and modules end to end: boot chain (MB1/MB2, UEFI), BPMP and device tree, pinmux, PCIe/USB/Ethernet, power profiles, and the drivers for robot hardware (EtherCAT, USB-C power delivery, Wi-Fi/Bluetooth, sensors, cameras)
* Help set the quality bar for the RT kernel and out-of-tree drivers: kernel configuration, ABI compatibility, and a plan to upstream changes or align with Meta's kernel instead of carrying long-lived patches
* Build the reliability and observability foundation: crash and kernel-log capture, symbolization, boot-time tracing, health telemetry, and fleet triage tooling, so that any robot failure can be diagnosed remotely

* Experience debugging hard cross-layer problems spanning hardware, firmware, kernel and user space

### **Preferred Qualifications:**

The Foundations Research team works on high-risk, high-reward ideas that could shape the next decade of AI. ---------------

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we're the people who keep the cloud running. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we're looking for talented people who want to help.

You'll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you'll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.  
  
Within AIS, the DC Robotics team is growing in maturity, so now is the time to join and drive game changing and rapid innovation used by AWS globally. Our designs will fundamentally change the data center, providing operational and financial benefits that are critical to the success of the AWS business and its millions of customers. Our engineers solve challenging technology problems and take big bets on new concepts, enabling AWS services to continue to revolutionize the industry. This role provides the opportunity to be a technical lead driving the innovations being developed and deployed in the next generation data centers.

You’ll work closely with research leads to translate scientific questions into rigorous studies, combining survey responses with behavioral data to understand how people’s experiences with AI evolve over time.

This is a hands-on role spanning applied analysis, research methods, and study execution. You’ll build reproducible analytical workflows, assess data quality and representativeness, and help establish reliable infrastructure for ongoing panel research. -----------

Pramaana Labs is a frontier AI lab building the verification layer for AI. Founded in 2025 and headquartered in Palo Alto, we turn complex human knowledge, including tax codes, legal rules, clinical guidelines and security protocols, into a formal representation, so every AI answer can be traced, challenged, and proved. Pramaana's architecture pairs foundation models trained to formalize and reason with a symbolic world model encoded in Lean 4. Pramaana was founded by a team out of Google, DeepMind, and Glean, combining frontier AI researchers and formal methods experts.

**The Role**

We’re looking for a full-stack engineer with focus on infrastructure to build the tools and systems that help Pramaana’s engineers and researchers develop, test, deploy, and operate their work more effectively.

This is an early-stage role with scope across the company. * **Improve tools through direct feedback.** Work alongside engineers and researchers to identify recurring problems, prioritize improvements, and measure whether tools reduce setup time, manual work, and failed runs. Maintain tests, documentation, and operational guidance for what you ship.

* Experience with infrastructure as code, container orchestration, or telemetry tooling, such as Terraform, Kubernetes, or OpenTelemetry.

--------------

Sift is the data infrastructure platform for hardware engineering teams. We turn high-frequency telemetry into engineering insights for mission-critical machines: rockets, satellites, autonomous vehicles, energy systems, and defense platforms. You'll design systems that allow engineers to spin up complete, production-like environments on demand to test changes, simulate real-world workloads, and validate correctness. As AI coding agents become increasingly integrated into development workflows, you'll build the infrastructure that enables these agents to independently test, debug, and validate the code they produce.  
Sift processes high-volume telemetry from complex hardware systems, making realistic testing environments particularly challenging. This is a foundational, high-ownership opportunity to architect and scale the infrastructure that powers how we develop, test, and ship software.

jobs.title: Infrastructure Software Engineer
jobs.description:
**About depthfirst**
--------------------

We believe that software is the foundation of modern civilization. Yet vulnerabilities threaten its integrity, security, and resilience. We are on a mission to secure the world's software.

depthfirst is building intelligence to detect and remediate critical software vulnerabilities. We are training and scaling security AI agents to discover zero-days vulnerabilities across large customer codebases and popular open source software.

Our founding team includes deep expertise in data, infrastructure, security and LLMs with technical leaders from DeepMind, Databricks, Square, and Faire. We are looking for strong technical people who are interested in working at the intersection of AI, Security, and Infrastructure.

**About This Role**
-------------------

We’re looking for an Infrastructure Software Engineer to build, scale, and secure the infrastructure that powers depthfirst. You’ll own our cloud and Kubernetes environments alongside the production services that manage sandboxes, orchestrate workloads, and control compute resources throughout their lifecycle.

This role combines deep infrastructure expertise with hands-on software engineering. You’ll design and develop infrastructure services and APIs, improve the reliability and efficiency of our systems, and strengthen the security of our compute environments. Your work will span application code, distributed systems, containers, networking, and cloud infrastructure.

You’ll own systems from architecture and implementation through deployment and ongoing operation. As depthfirst grows, you’ll shape how we scale our platform while keeping it reliable, secure, and straightforward to operate.

**You’re excited about this role because you will…**
----------------------------------------------------

* Build and operate the cloud infrastructure and Kubernetes clusters that support our production systems and engineering teams.

* Improve workload scheduling, autoscaling, and capacity management to support growing and variable demand.
* Strengthen infrastructure security through workload isolation, access controls, network policies, and secure configuration.
* Improve performance and cost efficiency by reducing startup latency, increasing resource utilization, and addressing system bottlenecks.
* Build observability and operational tooling that help engineers understand system behavior and resolve problems quickly.

* Strong software engineering skills in a language such as Go, with experience designing, building, and maintaining production services.

jobs.title: Compiler Frontend Engineer
jobs.description:
**Normal Computing | Build with Us**
------------------------------------

Normal is an applied AI company solving the hardest problems in AI and silicon. We build foundational hardware and software for the semiconductor industry, critical AI infrastructure, and the broader systems that power our world, in partnership with the world's most advanced institutions. We work as one team across New York City, Silicon Valley (Mountain View), London, Copenhagen, and Seoul.

**The Role**
------------

Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. Our compiler is how models reach that hardware, and new LLM architectures show up faster than most compilers can track. A new attention variant, MoE routing scheme, or quantization approach has to be represented faithfully in our compiler before it can run, let alone run fast. As a Compiler Engineer focused on frontend and model bring-up, you will extend our IR, ops, and lowering passes so new LLM architectures are supported before a customer asks for them.

This is a research-adjacent seat: you are expected to follow the literature closely, and publish on behalf of Normal. Our chip is pre-silicon, so you will validate bring-up against our simulators and FPGA prototypes first, so that models are ready to run when silicon arrives.

**What You Will Own**
---------------------

* **Model Bring-up**: Bring up frontend and mid-level support for new LLM architectures in our compiler, from attention variants to MoE routing schemes. Success means new architectures run correctly on our stack soon after release, ahead of customer demand.
* **IR and Lowering**: Extend our IR, ops, and lowering passes to represent new architectural primitives faithfully rather than approximately, with test coverage that keeps them correct as the compiler evolves.
* **Quantization and Numerics**: Represent the quantization schemes and numeric formats new models use, so lowering preserves model accuracy.
* **Architecture Tracking**: Track the LLM architecture landscape closely enough to recommend what the team brings up next.
* **Cross-Team Handoffs**: Hand lowered programs to the backend compiler engineers who map them onto our hardware, and work with our LLM serving engineer to take new models from compiler support to serving.

**What Makes You a Great Fit**
------------------------------

* Hands-on ML compiler experience: you have written and shipped compiler passes
* Deep familiarity with PyTorch internals, ideally including its compilation stack (TorchDynamo, FX, torch.export)
* Working knowledge of modern LLM architectures at the level of attention mechanisms, MoE routing, and quantization schemes
* Patience for the unglamorous part of the job: getting a new architecture from “runs” to “runs correctly” to “runs correctly and fast”
* Comfort designing compiler infrastructure in a young codebase as well as extending an established one
* Comfort building software for hardware that is still evolving, from simulation through bring-up
* Fluency in Python, and familiarity with C++ or Rust

**Bonus Points**
----------------

* Experience with other ML compilers, such as IREE, XLA, or TVM

jobs.description:
**About the Role**
  
  
Agentic Pods is building a new model for how Engineering partners with teams across Uber to transform work with AI. Our engineers embed directly with operational teams to understand complex workflows, reimagine how that work could operate in an agentic-first world, and build the production systems that make that future real.
  
  
We are looking for an Agentic Software Engineer to design, build, and operate production-grade agentic systems and processes that improve complex operational workflows.
  
  
This role combines backend engineering, reliability engineering, and a forward-deployed working model. You will work directly with operators and domain experts to discover opportunities, determine where agents can safely help, and turn ambiguous problems into reliable software.
  
  
You will own solutions from discovery through architecture, implementation, production rollout, and ongoing operation.
  
  
**What You Will Do**
  
  
**Discover and Build Agentic Systems**

* Embed with operational teams to understand workflows and identify where agentic AI, deterministic software, automation, or human decision-making can meaningfully improve how work gets done.
* Design, build, and iterate on production agentic systems, including agents, skills, backend services, APIs, integrations, data pipelines, and human-in-the-loop workflows, alongside real users.

**Own Production Reliability**

* Define reliability and quality targets and build observability across agent decisions, model behavior, dependencies, and workflow outcomes through tracing, logging, metrics, alerting, fallbacks, and recovery.
* Own systems in production, using incidents, operational data, and user outcomes to continuously improve performance, resilience, and reliability.

**Make Agents Safe and Measurable**

* Define evaluations and validation approaches for task completion, output quality, tool selection, policy compliance, and failure handling across offline testing, controlled rollouts, and production monitoring.
* Build appropriate controls-including permissions, approvals, auditability, data minimization, reversible execution, and human escalation-and partner with Security, Privacy, Legal, and Data to ensure consequential actions are safe, explainable, and recoverable.

**Build for Reuse and Scale**

* Identify capabilities that should become reusable skills, shared services, platform components, or standard integration patterns, supporting business and regional differences through configuration rather than unnecessary system forks.
* Establish common contracts and contribute to architecture, tooling, deployment patterns, reliability practices, and technical standards that enable Agentic Pods to build and scale consistently.

**Who Thrives on This Team**
  
  
We're looking for engineers with strong technical depth who are comfortable operating in ambiguity and working directly with users.

* **Agentic-first thinker:** You naturally look for opportunities to redesign workflows around what's newly possible.
* **0 1 builder:** You move quickly from ambiguous problems to working software.
* **Product-minded:** You have strong judgment about what is useful and worth building, not just what is technically possible.
* **Systems thinker:** You recognize when individual solutions should become reusable capabilities or standards.
* **Adaptable communicator:** You learn unfamiliar domains quickly, build trust, and communicate effectively with technical and non-technical partners.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree or equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics or related field OR 1-year full-time Software Engineering work experience, WHICH INCLUDES 1-year total technical software engineering experience in one or more of the following areas:
  + Programming language (e.g., C, C++, Java, Python, or Go).
* Note: The 1-year total of specialized software engineering experience may have been gained through education and full-time work experience, additional training, coursework, research, or similar (or some combination of these). The year of specialized experience is not necessarily in addition to the years of education and full-time work experience indicated.
* Strong experience designing and building production backend or distributed systems, including agentic applications, AI-enabled workflows, orchestration systems, developer platforms, APIs, asynchronous workflows, and system integrations.
* Experience owning and improving production systems, including monitoring, alerting, incident response, failure recovery, and debugging across application, infrastructure, and data dependencies.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience integrating LLMs with tools, APIs, enterprise data, and permissioned systems.
* Familiarity with agent evaluation, retrieval, context management, model routing, and safety controls.
* Experience in SRE, infrastructure, platform, production engineering, or a forward-deployed/embedded engineering model.
* Experience designing systems for sensitive or operationally consequential workflows.
* Ability to lead technical design, drive key architectural decisions, and influence technical direction across teams.

jobs.description:
**Hadrian - Manufacturing the Future**
======================================

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.

Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.

Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.

If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.

**The Role**

Candidates for this role could end up working with a number of our internal products and teams:

***Flow*** is Hadrian’s FactoryOS, our core platform comprised of a variety of applications that model, manage, and automate an extremely complex network of factories.

***Copilot***is our suite of manufacturing automation products which automates or accelerates key processes within the factory including quoting, CAM programming, and CMM programming.

***Factory Automation***develops robotic cells for use in our factories and the software that controls them.

We have a broad set of applications internally. Candidates interested in redefining manufacturing software will have ample opportunity to do so.

**What You’ll Do**

* Scope, architect, implement, and deploy critical applications across multiple product verticals.
* Engage in product discovery alongside experts in manufacturing and software- help define what needs to exist and what needs to be better.
* Build alongside an incredible team of engineers and operators.

**What We’re Looking For**

* Expert in TypeScript and frontend web development, ideally using React and related state management solutions. Deep understanding of the frontend ecosystem.
* Strong ability and desire to write high quality code and maintain a high quality codebase.
* API design experience (REST & gRPC).
* Know how to develop, deploy, and maintain fullstack applications using a modern web stack.
* Bias towards action and take pride in your work.
* Excited to work in a fast-paced environment with high-stakes and quick iteration cycles.

**What Will Set You Apart**

* Have great product intuition and user empathy. You enjoy talking to users.
* Have a strong sense of design and execute at a high level with or without design support.
* Comfortable jumping into different areas of our stack as needed: Go, Python, C#, C++, etc.
* Have experience with data visualization, video games, CAD/CAM software, or 3D environments.
* Have demonstrated success with developing and deploying high performance web applications.

**Logistics**

This role is based out of our Los Angeles (Torrance) or San Francisco Bay Area office.

**Compensation**

For this role, the target salary range is $220,000 - $320,000(actual range may vary based on experience).

This is the lowest to highest salary we reasonably and in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range, and the range may be modified in the future. An employee's pay position within the salary range will be based on several factors, including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

**Benefits for Full-time Employees**
------------------------------------

* Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees
    
  401k
* Relocation support may be provided for certain situations, based on business need.
* Flexible vacation policy
* Equity

**ITAR Requirements**
---------------------

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen or national, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

**Use of AI in hiring**
-----------------------

Hadrian uses AI-assisted tools in our recruiting and hiring processes to help our team work more efficiently. This may include tools that help organize and analyze recruiting data, as well as an AI-powered notetaker that can record and transcribe interviews and help coordinate feedback. These tools support our team and are not used to make hiring decisions. All candidate evaluations and hiring decisions are performed by humans. If an interview will be recorded, you will be notified in advance and may opt out at any time with no impact on your candidacy. Candidate data processed through these tools is subject to the same protections described in our Privacy Policy.

**Consideration of Criminal History**
-------------------------------------

Hadrian will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of all applicable laws. We do not ask about criminal history on our application, and we do not consider criminal history before making a conditional offer of employment.

**Hadrian Is An Equal Opportunity Employer**
--------------------------------------------

Hadrian does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability

jobs.description:
**About the Role**  
  
The Marketplace Fares Team powers global fares for all of Uber - that's all riders, drivers, eaters, new initiatives and technical consumers. Tens of billions of dollars in gross bookings flow through the systems and experiences within our responsibility. Our scope and critical work spans the entire stack - from platform fare calculation for riders and drivers, to data science prediction of trustworthy upfront prices, to compelling mobile fare experiences for our customers. Fares is a backend team with two product-centric tracks (Rider Fares & Driver Fares) and multiple platform-centric tracks (Fares Platform, Intelligence, Experiences, and Solutions). On this team, you'll work closely with product, operations, data science, and engineering teams throughout the company.
  
  
As a backend engineer you will make an impact in the real world using exciting and new technology. You will work on a fast-paced solutions oriented marketplace team, looking to create robust and powerful features that power the critical internal configuration platform for Fares @ Uber. Your ability to work closely with other engineers, product managers, and product operations teams will bring the best experiences possible in an exciting environment.
  
  
**About the Team**  
  
The Marketplace organization at Uber tackles some of the hardest quantitative problems related to improving Uber's realtime marketplace which deeply impact the everyday experiences of our riders and driver partners. The Marketplace teams focus on building technology to achieve market balance (matching the supply of drivers with demand from riders) and optimize the reliability and availability of Uber's trip fulfillment. We are the brain of Uber, tackling the company's most challenging quantitative problems: optimizing Uber's dynamic pricing system; providing real time positioning guidance to drivers; optimizing dispatches of drivers and couriers to incoming requests; matching riders together for UberPool, and many more.
  
  
**What You'll Do**  
  
As a member of the Marketplace Fares team, you will be doing just that: building out and expanding our powerful Fares backend systems to help build features and drive key new product launches at Uber.

* You will be responsible for development of our framework infrastructure to improve our ability to customize our fare configurations for every Uber business and market need.
* You will have a deep understanding of the problems our platform solves for. You will also get to work with many different parts of the company in helping drive projects that impact millions of customers.
* Participate in periodic on-call rotations and be available for critical issues.

**Basic Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems or a similar field
* Strong coding/debugging abilities with at least one coding language. We primarily work with Go and Python.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* 4+ years of total software development experience as a backend developer
* Proven experience building highly available distributed systems (at Uber scale) and working across multiple backend services
* Experience working on scalable backend systems utilizing a microservices architecture
* High bar for quality as demonstrated by code reviews, documentation, unit and integration testing
Background in payments/fintech engineering  

  
  
For San Francisco, CA-based roles: The base salary range for this role is USD $171,000 per year - USD $190,000 per year.  
  
For Sunnyvale, CA-based roles: The base salary range for this role is USD $171,000 per year - USD $190,000 per year.  
  
For all US locations, you will be eligible to participate in Uber's bonus program, and may be offered an equity award & other types of comp. All full-time employees are eligible to participate in a 401(k) plan. You will also be eligible for various benefits.  
  
**Ready to Ride?**  
  
This isn't the kind of place where you follow a playbook - it's where you help write one. If you're driven by impact, energized by challenge, and ready to shape how the world moves - we'd love to hear from you.  
  
You may be eligible for bonuses, equity, and other compensation, as well as a range of benefits. Explore our benefits.  
  
Offices remain key to collaboration and Uber's culture. Unless approved for full remote work, employees must spend at least 50% of their time in-office. Some roles, like those at greenlight hubs, require full-time in-office presence. Ask your Recruiter for details about this role's requirements.  
  
Uber is proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know by completing this form.

---------------

Project Kuiper is an initiative to launch a constellation of Low Earth Orbit satellites that will provide low-latency, high-speed broadband connectivity to unserved and underserved communities around the world.  
Come work at Amazon!  
  
As a member of Kuiper MAC-SW, you will be responsible for delivering embedded FW code running on ground networks on customer terminals and on satellites. Come and join the innovative and unique wireless project Kuiper. You would be focused on designing, developing and testing complete Kuiper-MAC FW. You will be a key member of a cross functional team of innovators, working on unique wireless technology that will enable millions of people to stay connected. Design, develop, integrate and bring up Kuiper-MAC FW components/drivers in a real-time embedded environment

Key job responsibilities  

* Working in a cross-functional environment to define multi-dimensional performance requirements (e.g., MIPs, memory BW)

* Build component use-cases/test-cases and debug your code in Kuiper embedded environment

**What is PlayerZero?**
-----------------------

Building great software takes more than writing code. It takes teams working together, and too often, the information they need is scattered across tools, conversations, and systems.

PlayerZero is an AI platform that connects work across enterprise Support, Engineering, Product, QA, and SRE teams, helping them resolve issues faster, improve software quality, and plan what to build next.

At its core is our Engineering World Model: a living understanding of a company’s software, how it runs, and the people and decisions behind it. By connecting codebases, tickets, production telemetry, and the conversations that shape the work, our model links what software is intended to do with how it actually behaves in production—and learns from where the two diverge.

Our agents (we call them Players :) use that context to take on work across the software lifecycle. They learn from each outcome, earning trust and taking on more responsibility over time.

We’re building a future where AI plays an active role in how teams plan, build, and run software. We’re looking for people across disciplines to help shape it.

**About the AI Infra team**
---------------------------

Most AI tools help one person perform a task faster, a session at a time. But real software work doesn’t happen in one session or one tool. A bug moves from a customer, to ticket, to a Slack thread to a PR to a deploy, across people and systems that never see the whole picture. The most interesting context lives between those systems of record, and so does the real work.

PlayerZero is the platform where that work gets done. At its core is a living model that connects everything a company’s software depends on: the code, the infrastructure it runs on, and the people and decisions behind it. Our agents use it to own real work across the entire SDLC, from fixing production issues to planning what gets built next. And because that work runs through our platform, they learn from every outcome and earn the right to do more.

The AI Infrastructure team builds the machine underneath: where agents execute, what context they access, and how work moves between agents and people. It has to be fast, composable, and built to scale.

**What you will do**
--------------------

We’re hiring infrastructure engineers who like hard distributed-systems problems and want to own them end to end. Here’s some of what you might work on with us:

* **Agentic infrastructure.** Our agents don’t answer a question and disappear. They take on units of work that run for hours or days, change hands, and continue to drive work to completion. We build the runtime that creates continuity for that work: long-running sessions that survive failures, durable workflow state, lifecycle and cancellation, and workflows that track each piece of work to completion across every stage and every party involved.
* **Context architecture.** Because work flows through our platform, we’re present when the connections between code, tickets, units of work, and past decisions are made. The context between these systems of record is necessary for the agent to do its work well, and the data models behind it shape everything an agent can know. We design how that context is represented and delivered: what gets precomputed ahead of time versus resolved on demand, and how the right slice reaches each agent at the right moment.
* **The communication layer**. Real work doesn’t happen in isolation. Agents work alongside other agents (subagents, teammates, agents on customer machines, agents over MCP) and alongside people. We’re building the layer that connects them: messaging between agents within and across sessions, escalations that pull in the right person at the right time, and agents that can be interrupted when new information arrives.
* **Sandboxes and fleets.** An organization’s work is spread across laptops, QA fleets, production hosts, and ephemeral scripts. We build our own sandbox infrastructure, environments that spin up instantly and run by the hundreds, plus a fleet layer that lets agents work on the machines where customer work already happens.

**What you bring**
------------------

* A builder mindset. You own projects end to end, think carefully about data models, performance, and maintainability, and have taken prototypes to production with a clear sense of the reliability and scale tradeoffs.
* 3–5+ years building backend systems, ideally real-time, stateful, or event-driven workloads, with strong distributed systems fundamentals: message queues (Kafka, Pulsar), distributed locks, pub/sub, and their failure modes.
* Experience building infrastructure for LLMs in production: tool calling, streaming, token budgets, or evaluation harnesses, and a sense of what agents need from the systems beneath them.
* Experience designing data models for messy, interconnected domains. You know how to structure data so it stays correct as it grows and changes, and you think about how it will be queried and served before you write the schema. You’ve made schema and storage decisions that held up under scale, and you know the cost of getting them wrong.
* You keep work moving. You balance speed of execution with code quality, unblock yourself when you can, and pull in the right people at the right time when you can’t.

**Bonus Points**
----------------

* Hands-on with vector databases (pgvector, Pinecone, Turbopuffer) or hybrid search systems
* Experience with Kotlin/JVM (our primary stack) or Rust, MongoDB, Postgres, or Redis, and WebSockets or other real-time patterns

* You’ve worked on filesystem layers such as FUSE, overlay filesystems, or remote-backed storage
* You’ve worked with event sourcing, lineage, or provenance data, where the record of what happened is itself a product

**About the role**
------------------

As a Site Reliability Engineer, you’ll improve the reliability, security, and visibility of PlayerZero’s production systems. You’ll combine hands-on AWS infrastructure operations with automation, monitoring, and application instrumentation to help engineers understand system behavior and resolve problems at their source.

You’ll partner closely with our existing SRE and engineering teams to operate distributed services and stateful data systems, reduce operational toil, and strengthen incident response. We’re looking for someone who can independently investigate complex issues, safely change production infrastructure, and follow improvements through to completion.

**What you will do**
--------------------

* **Operate production infrastructure and data systems.** Maintain AWS environments and systems such as Kafka, Pulsar, and Valkey, including upgrades, replication health, rolling restarts, and failover.
* **Automate operational work.** Build tools and workflows that eliminate repetitive tasks, reduce manual intervention, and make production operations more consistent.
* **Improve monitoring and instrumentation.** Work with engineers to instrument application code and strengthen metrics, logs, distributed tracing, dashboards, and actionable alerts.
* **Troubleshoot and respond to incidents.** Investigate problems across applications, infrastructure, networking, and data systems. Help restore service and turn findings into lasting fixes and useful runbooks.
* **Make infrastructure changes and deployments safer.** Partner with Platform and application engineers on infrastructure as code, CI/CD, configuration management, rollback practices, and production readiness.
* **Keep production systems secure and current.** Perform OS and kernel patching, remediate infrastructure vulnerabilities within agreed timelines, and execute safe rolling maintenance.
* **Improve performance and resilience.** Identify bottlenecks and failure modes, assess capacity needs, and help establish practical service health indicators and reliability targets.

**What you bring**
------------------

* Experience independently operating, troubleshooting, and improving production services in an SRE, production engineering, or similar role.
* Hands-on AWS production experience, including EC2, VPC networking, IAM, Auto Scaling Groups, and Systems Manager, ideally across multiple accounts.
* Strong fundamentals in Linux, networking, and distributed systems.
* Experience operating distributed data systems such as Kafka, Pulsar, or Redis/Valkey, including upgrades, rolling restarts, replication, and failover.
* Strong programming or scripting skills, with experience building operational automation and improving application instrumentation.
* Experience with metrics, logs, distributed tracing, and alerting, including OpenTelemetry or comparable instrumentation.
* Production experience with infrastructure as code, preferably Terraform, including safely modifying existing infrastructure and state, alongside CI/CD, containers, and repeatable deployment practices.
* Experience responding to production incidents, performing maintenance, and following through on corrective actions.
* Clear communication, sound judgment under pressure, and a collaborative approach to solving problems across teams.
* Experience supporting compliance programs such as SOC 2 or HIPAA, including maintaining technical controls and producing evidence, is also valuable.

**What success looks like**
---------------------------

Production services and data systems remain healthy through growth, releases, and maintenance. Engineers detect and diagnose problems faster, recurring issues and manual tasks decrease, and infrastructure changes are predictable and recoverable. Incidents lead to lasting improvements, and security maintenance stays current.

**Why PlayerZero**
------------------

PlayerZero is an early leader in AI-powered production engineering, defining how enterprises use AI to understand, improve, and operate their software.

We’re a small team with meaningful problems to solve and room for each person to make their mark. Whether you’re building the technology, working with customers, or growing the business, you’ll help shape the product, the company, and what customers expect from this emerging category.

If you’re excited by work where the answers aren’t all written yet, and want a hand in writing them, you’ll fit right in.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Agentic
jobs.description:
**About the Role**
  
  
Agentic Pods is building a new model for how Engineering partners with teams across Uber to transform work with AI. Our engineers embed directly with operational teams to understand complex workflows, reimagine how that work could operate in an agentic-first world, and build the production systems that make that future real.
  
  
We are looking for an Agentic Software Engineer to design, build, and operate production-grade agentic systems and processes that improve complex operational workflows.
  
  
This role combines backend engineering, reliability engineering, and a forward-deployed working model. You will work directly with operators and domain experts to discover opportunities, determine where agents can safely help, and turn ambiguous problems into reliable software.
  
  
You will own solutions from discovery through architecture, implementation, production rollout, and ongoing operation.
  
  
**What You Will Do**
  
  
**Discover and Build Agentic Systems**

* Embed with operational teams to understand workflows and identify where agentic AI, deterministic software, automation, or human decision-making can meaningfully improve how work gets done.
* Design, build, and iterate on production agentic systems, including agents, skills, backend services, APIs, integrations, data pipelines, and human-in-the-loop workflows, alongside real users.

**Own Production Reliability**

* Define reliability and quality targets and build observability across agent decisions, model behavior, dependencies, and workflow outcomes through tracing, logging, metrics, alerting, fallbacks, and recovery.
* Own systems in production, using incidents, operational data, and user outcomes to continuously improve performance, resilience, and reliability.

**Make Agents Safe and Measurable**

* Define evaluations and validation approaches for task completion, output quality, tool selection, policy compliance, and failure handling across offline testing, controlled rollouts, and production monitoring.
* Build appropriate controls-including permissions, approvals, auditability, data minimization, reversible execution, and human escalation-and partner with Security, Privacy, Legal, and Data to ensure consequential actions are safe, explainable, and recoverable.

**Build for Reuse and Scale**

* Identify capabilities that should become reusable skills, shared services, platform components, or standard integration patterns, supporting business and regional differences through configuration rather than unnecessary system forks.
* Establish common contracts and contribute to architecture, tooling, deployment patterns, reliability practices, and technical standards that enable Agentic Pods to build and scale consistently.

**Who Thrives on This Team**
  
  
We're looking for engineers with strong technical depth who are comfortable operating in ambiguity and working directly with users.

* **Agentic-first thinker:** You naturally look for opportunities to redesign workflows around what's newly possible.
* **0 1 builder:** You move quickly from ambiguous problems to working software.
* **Product-minded:** You have strong judgment about what is useful and worth building, not just what is technically possible.
* **Systems thinker:** You recognize when individual solutions should become reusable capabilities or standards.

On any given day at Disney Entertainment & ESPN Technology, we’re reimagining ways to create magical viewing experiences for the world’s most beloved stories while also transforming our media business for the future. Whether that’s evolving our streaming and digital products in new and immersive ways, powering worldwide advertising and distribution to enhance flexibility and efficiency, or delivering Disney’s unmatched entertainment and sports content, every day is a moment to make a difference to partners and to hundreds of millions of people around the world.

A few reasons why we think you’d love working here:

* **Building the future of Disney’s media:** DE&E Technologists are designing and building the infrastructure that will power our media, advertising, and distribution businesses for years to come.
* **Reach & Scale:** The products and platforms this group builds and operates delight millions of consumers every minute of every day – from Disney+ and Hulu, to ABC News and Entertainment, to ESPN and ESPN+, and much more.
* **Innovation:** We develop and implement groundbreaking products and techniques that shape industry norms and enhance how audiences experience sports, entertainment & news.

**Job Summary**

The **Cannonball squad** sits within MarTech Tools in Commerce & Identity (Commerce – Acquire). We build internal platforms that power how Disney Streaming markets and publishes to hundreds of millions of unauthenticated visitors across Disney+, Hulu, ESPN+, and Star+.

Cannonball is the enterprise CMS and publish engine for marketing landing pages and related experiences. Editors use it to model content, author in a rich entry editor, schedule and bulk-publish, and roll out localized variants globally.

* **Magic Frame:** Source for incoming assets and templates
* **Royalball:** Editorial content workflow management
* **Nexus / Web Growth:** Delivery pipeline for published end-user experiences
* **Pixelball & Wayback:** Experience validation and historical archiving

Product Marketing, Paid Media, Marketing Design, SEO, Ad Ops, Legal, and Customer Support all depend on this stack to ship campaigns faster with built-in governance. * Solid understanding of JavaScript or TypeScript and core web fundamentals (HTML/CSS, HTTP, REST, browser devtools).

* Comfort learning within a large codebase and proactively seeking guidance.
* Clear written and verbal communication skills; ability to work effectively in a hybrid, cross-functional team.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Exposure to Vue, React, or another modern SPA framework.
* Familiarity with Git version control, code reviews, and CI/CD workflows (GitHub Actions or similar).
* Experience with automated testing (unit, integration, or E2E).
* Interest in CMS platforms, content modeling, localization, or marketing technology.

**Required Education**

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a comparable field of study, or equivalent work experience

new_jobs.title: Research Engineer, Algorithms
new_jobs.description:
**Normal Computing | Build with Us**
------------------------------------

Normal is an applied AI company solving the hardest problems in AI and silicon. We build foundational hardware and software for the semiconductor industry, critical AI infrastructure, and the broader systems that power our world, in partnership with the world's most advanced institutions. We work as one team across New York City, Silicon Valley (Mountain View), London, Copenhagen, and Seoul.

**The Role**
------------

Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. You will develop the computational methods that make LLM inference run efficiently on it. The core challenge is rethinking how operations like attention, memory access, and long-context decoding should behave on hardware that computes inside memory, rather than adapting standard GPU kernels to a new chip.

Your job is to develop the algorithms that exploit this natively: understand which parts of LLM workloads are best suited to in-memory execution, design numerical methods that map onto the hardware's physical behavior, and validate them against our simulators and FPGA prototypes first, and against silicon as it arrives.

This is a co-design role. The hardware and the algorithms are developed in parallel, which means you will influence architectural decisions rather than implement against a fixed specification. The strongest candidates have a deep understanding of both large model inference and the mathematics of stochastic systems, and have built systems that run on real hardware.

**What You Will Own**
---------------------

* **Algorithm Development:** Develop algorithms for LLM inference workloads running on our in-memory hardware. Success means algorithms that measurably improve LLM inference on our hardware, demonstrated in simulation and then on silicon.
* **Software/Hardware Co-Design:** Work directly with hardware and architecture teams to shape what the chip can and should compute natively.
* **Numerical Methods:** Design numerical methods that exploit thermal noise and analog dynamics rather than working around them.
* **Evaluation & Benchmarks:** Build evaluation frameworks and benchmarks that characterize algorithm behavior on real hardware or simulation.
* **Workload Translation:** Translate insights about model workloads into constraints and opportunities for hardware design.
* **Rapid Prototyping:** Prototype and iterate rapidly as hardware evolves from simulation to silicon.
* **Performance Optimization:** Optimize performance at both the gate level and the algorithmic level.

**What Makes You a Great Fit**
------------------------------

* Deep understanding of large model inference: attention mechanisms, KV cache, long-context decoding, memory bandwidth constraints
* Experience with inference optimization: quantization, sparsity, kernel fusion, or memory-efficient attention
* Familiarity with stochastic systems, probabilistic methods, numerical analysis, or analog computation
* Experience implementing algorithms close to hardware, beyond high-level frameworks
* Comfort reasoning from first principles about what a novel substrate can do efficiently
* Track record of taking ideas from theory to working implementation on real hardware
* Strong programming skills in Python and at least one systems language
* Collaborative instinct and ability to work across hardware, architecture, and software teams

**Bonus Points**
----------------

* PhD in machine learning, applied mathematics, physics, electrical engineering, or a related field
* Exposure to analog or mixed-signal systems, in-memory compute, or non-von-Neumann architectures
* Experience working on hardware that did not yet exist when you joined
* Publications or open-source work in efficient inference, stochastic algorithms, or novel computing

***Equal Employment Opportunity Statement***

*Normal Computing is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected status.*

***Accessibility Accommodations***

*Normal Computing is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please let us know at accommodations@normalcomputing.com.*

***Privacy Notice***

*By submitting your application, you agree that Normal Computing may collect, use, and store your personal information for employment-related purposes in accordance with our* *Applicant Privacy Notice**.*

depthfirst is building intelligence to detect and remediate critical software vulnerabilities. We are training and scaling security AI agents to discover zero-days vulnerabilities across large customer codebases and popular open source software.

new_jobs.title: Compiler Frontend Engineer
new_jobs.description:
**Normal Computing | Build with Us**
------------------------------------

Normal is an applied AI company solving the hardest problems in AI and silicon. We build foundational hardware and software for the semiconductor industry, critical AI infrastructure, and the broader systems that power our world, in partnership with the world's most advanced institutions. We work as one team across New York City, Silicon Valley (Mountain View), London, Copenhagen, and Seoul.

**The Role**
------------

Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. Our compiler is how models reach that hardware, and new LLM architectures show up faster than most compilers can track. A new attention variant, MoE routing scheme, or quantization approach has to be represented faithfully in our compiler before it can run, let alone run fast. As a Compiler Engineer focused on frontend and model bring-up, you will extend our IR, ops, and lowering passes so new LLM architectures are supported before a customer asks for them.

This is a research-adjacent seat: you are expected to follow the literature closely, and publish on behalf of Normal. Our chip is pre-silicon, so you will validate bring-up against our simulators and FPGA prototypes first, so that models are ready to run when silicon arrives.

**What You Will Own**
---------------------

* **Model Bring-up**: Bring up frontend and mid-level support for new LLM architectures in our compiler, from attention variants to MoE routing schemes. Success means new architectures run correctly on our stack soon after release, ahead of customer demand.
* **IR and Lowering**: Extend our IR, ops, and lowering passes to represent new architectural primitives faithfully rather than approximately, with test coverage that keeps them correct as the compiler evolves.
* **Quantization and Numerics**: Represent the quantization schemes and numeric formats new models use, so lowering preserves model accuracy.
* **Architecture Tracking**: Track the LLM architecture landscape closely enough to recommend what the team brings up next.
* **Cross-Team Handoffs**: Hand lowered programs to the backend compiler engineers who map them onto our hardware, and work with our LLM serving engineer to take new models from compiler support to serving.

**What Makes You a Great Fit**
------------------------------

* Hands-on ML compiler experience: you have written and shipped compiler passes
* Deep familiarity with PyTorch internals, ideally including its compilation stack (TorchDynamo, FX, torch.export)
* Working knowledge of modern LLM architectures at the level of attention mechanisms, MoE routing, and quantization schemes
* Patience for the unglamorous part of the job: getting a new architecture from “runs” to “runs correctly” to “runs correctly and fast”
* Comfort designing compiler infrastructure in a young codebase as well as extending an established one
* Comfort building software for hardware that is still evolving, from simulation through bring-up
* Fluency in Python, and familiarity with C++ or Rust

**Bonus Points**
----------------

* Experience with other ML compilers, such as IREE, XLA, or TVM
* Familiarity with other ML frameworks and graph formats, such as JAX or ONNX
* Experience partitioning models across devices with tensor, pipeline, or expert parallelism
* Experience with hardware-software co-design
* Experience with non-standard or in-memory hardware targets
* Contributions to open-source compiler or ML infrastructure projects

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected status.*

**What is PlayerZero?**
-----------------------

Building great software takes more than writing code. It takes teams working together, and too often, the information they need is scattered across tools, conversations, and systems.

PlayerZero is an AI platform that connects work across enterprise Support, Engineering, Product, QA, and SRE teams, helping them resolve issues faster, improve software quality, and plan what to build next.

At its core is our Engineering World Model: a living understanding of a company’s software, how it runs, and the people and decisions behind it. By connecting codebases, tickets, production telemetry, and the conversations that shape the work, our model links what software is intended to do with how it actually behaves in production—and learns from where the two diverge.

Our agents (we call them Players :) use that context to take on work across the software lifecycle. They learn from each outcome, earning trust and taking on more responsibility over time.

We’re building a future where AI plays an active role in how teams plan, build, and run software. We’re looking for people across disciplines to help shape it.

**About the AI Infra team**
---------------------------

Most AI tools help one person perform a task faster, a session at a time. But real software work doesn’t happen in one session or one tool. A bug moves from a customer, to ticket, to a Slack thread to a PR to a deploy, across people and systems that never see the whole picture. The most interesting context lives between those systems of record, and so does the real work.

PlayerZero is the platform where that work gets done. At its core is a living model that connects everything a company’s software depends on: the code, the infrastructure it runs on, and the people and decisions behind it. Our agents use it to own real work across the entire SDLC, from fixing production issues to planning what gets built next. And because that work runs through our platform, they learn from every outcome and earn the right to do more.

The AI Infrastructure team builds the machine underneath: where agents execute, what context they access, and how work moves between agents and people. It has to be fast, composable, and built to scale.

**What you will do**
--------------------

We’re hiring infrastructure engineers who like hard distributed-systems problems and want to own them end to end. Here’s some of what you might work on with us:

* **Agentic infrastructure.** Our agents don’t answer a question and disappear. They take on units of work that run for hours or days, change hands, and continue to drive work to completion. We build the runtime that creates continuity for that work: long-running sessions that survive failures, durable workflow state, lifecycle and cancellation, and workflows that track each piece of work to completion across every stage and every party involved.
* **Context architecture.** Because work flows through our platform, we’re present when the connections between code, tickets, units of work, and past decisions are made. The context between these systems of record is necessary for the agent to do its work well, and the data models behind it shape everything an agent can know. We design how that context is represented and delivered: what gets precomputed ahead of time versus resolved on demand, and how the right slice reaches each agent at the right moment.
* **The communication layer**. Real work doesn’t happen in isolation. Agents work alongside other agents (subagents, teammates, agents on customer machines, agents over MCP) and alongside people. We’re building the layer that connects them: messaging between agents within and across sessions, escalations that pull in the right person at the right time, and agents that can be interrupted when new information arrives.
* **Sandboxes and fleets.** An organization’s work is spread across laptops, QA fleets, production hosts, and ephemeral scripts. We build our own sandbox infrastructure, environments that spin up instantly and run by the hundreds, plus a fleet layer that lets agents work on the machines where customer work already happens.

**What you bring**
------------------

* A builder mindset. You own projects end to end, think carefully about data models, performance, and maintainability, and have taken prototypes to production with a clear sense of the reliability and scale tradeoffs.
* 3–5+ years building backend systems, ideally real-time, stateful, or event-driven workloads, with strong distributed systems fundamentals: message queues (Kafka, Pulsar), distributed locks, pub/sub, and their failure modes.
* Experience building infrastructure for LLMs in production: tool calling, streaming, token budgets, or evaluation harnesses, and a sense of what agents need from the systems beneath them.
* Experience designing data models for messy, interconnected domains. You know how to structure data so it stays correct as it grows and changes, and you think about how it will be queried and served before you write the schema. You’ve made schema and storage decisions that held up under scale, and you know the cost of getting them wrong.
* You keep work moving. You balance speed of execution with code quality, unblock yourself when you can, and pull in the right people at the right time when you can’t.

**Bonus Points**

* Hands-on with vector databases (pgvector, Pinecone, Turbopuffer) or hybrid search systems
* Experience with Kotlin/JVM (our primary stack) or Rust, MongoDB, Postgres, or Redis, and WebSockets or other real-time patterns

* You’ve worked with event sourcing, lineage, or provenance data, where the record of what happened is itself a product
